title.narrative: TetraPak & FAO: Dairy network in Colombia (peacebuilding)

description.narrative: FAO-projektet inom offentlig-privat utvecklingspartnerskap i allians med Tetra Pak och det colombianska privata företaget Alpina är treårigt. Syftet är att bidra till att stärka ett hållbart och replikerbart mejeriproduktionssystem för småskaliga bönder i kommunerna Cajibio, Totoro, Silvia och Sotará i Cauca-departementet (Colombia). Projektet bedöms vara i linje med Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Colombia 2021-2025. Stödet är huvudsakligen inom Konflikt, Fred och Säkerhet, med sekundära mål är inom miljö och jämställdhet.

This is a FAO led project and public-private development partnership in alliance with Tetra Pak and the Colombian private company Alpina. The aim of the project is to contribute to the strengthening of a sustainable and replicable dairy production system for small scale farmers in the municipalities of Cajibio, Totoro, Silvia and Sotará in the Department of Cauca (Colombia). The principal objective is Conflict, Peace and Security, Gender and Environment.

The main goal is contributing to the implementation of the first part of the peace agreement (Integral Rural Reform 1.3.3) and the Colombian National Development Plan through the strengthening of a sustainable and replicable dairy production system using a public-private development partnership with small scale farmers in the municipalities of Cajibio, Totoro, Silvia and Sotará in the Department of Cauca.
The specific objectives are:
1.Prioritized communities of small livestock farmers in the Department of Cauca have appropriated practices associated with Sustainable Community livestock farming, thereby transforming their productive, social and commercial processes.
2.Communities and institutions in prioritized regions have implemented environmentally sustainable practices and ecosystem management tools linked to Sustainable Community Livestock Farming.
3.Communities of small-scale producers/farmers have increased productivity and competitiveness of their sustainable farming enterprises/associations with an emphasis on milk production.
4.The local community actors have implemented a territorial information system thereby strengthening their milk collection processes and supporting an integrated territorial transformation.

description.narrative:
This project was officially launched in August 2023 with the signature of the agreement with FAO and was formally presented to national and local authorities in a public event with media.
As mentioned in the statement on narrative report (UM2022/26989/BOGO/33) during the period from January to December 2024, FAO has achieved concrete results and made significant progress in all the expected outputs. The Embassy´s assessment is that FAO has established strategic dialogue and coordinated commitments with 43 stakeholders, demonstrating the important articulating and complementary role of international cooperation in building on previous experiences in Cauca and other regions.
The first output, "Prioritized communities of small livestock farmers in the Department of Cauca have adopted sustainable community livestock farming practices, thereby transforming their productive, social, and commercial processes," is 50% complete. The second output of Communities and institutions have implemented environmentally sustainable practices and ecosystem management tools, is 39% completed. The third output, "Communities of small-scale producers/farmers have increased the productivity and competitiveness of their sustainable farming enterprises/associations," is 22% completed. The fourth output: The local community actors have implemented a territorial information system thereby strengthening their milk collection processes and supporting an integrated territorial transformation has 13% of progress.
The first activity implemented was the baseline collection to analyze the quantity and quality of milk produced, the costs analysis, the commercial processes, the gender and environmental issues. Then, a specific action plan was proposed for 398 participating families. 24 agreements with 24 reference farms were signed, considering their strategic location and participant´s commitment. The action plan also started with the creation of committees and productions hubs that implements the horizontal governance structures. Other important result was the creation of sustainable schools networks that includes 304 participants (teachers and students. 158 men and 146 women) from 5 local schools to Integrate academic training with practical agricultural knowledge and adapt teaching methods to the realities and challenges of the context. In addition, they have created 5 communication groups (one for each municipality and two in Silvia), including young participants
Participants have started with common planning to promote ecological connectivity between farms. In the production hubs they have started learning about agroecological production, soil fertilization, silvopastoral systems, animal nutrition among others. On average, the 33 nodes have already produced 200 litters of organic liquid fertilizers. Nearly 60% of participating families have reduced their use of chemical inputs, through composting and using natural plant care products.
In terms of water conservation, 68% of the nodes protect water sources through strategic isolation, and 15% have re-forested areas around bodies of water. In the 21 reference farms they have started seeding silvopastoral systems with native species, adapted to each altitude. They have changed 45 hectares of traditional grasslands to silvopastoral systems with approximately 50,000 linear meters of living fences that incorporate native species. These interventions improve productivity, connect forest fragments, and increase biodiversity. Six nurseries have been established to date, and the goal is to reach 24 nurseries.
Participants received training in financial instruments, production costs, associativity, animal care among other issues. At the technical production level, the committees have made progress in evaluating milk quality parameters with the support of the commercial ally, ALIVAL. They have identified production and quality factors and implemented guidelines and improvement practices, achieving better quality and price indicators. According to the results analysis from ALIVAL, a global analysis showed a 34.5% increase in hygiene quality (CFU). In addition, with the technical support in the following areas: 1. Feed and Nutritional Management, 2. Forage; 3. Milk Quality and Handling; 4. Animal Health; 5. Fertility and Reproduction; 6. Farm Management, there was an increase of 6.06 liters/hectare/day to 6.73 liters/hectare/day. This represents an 11.06% increase, compared to the baseline. Finally, with the training in financial education, they have already created 6 rotary funds with more than $92million COP in savings.
In March 2024 and March 2025, the Embassy accompany territorial workshops where a fluent dialogue with the local authorities, universities, local producers and national institutions working in Cauca were held. These field visits were also evidence of the achieved results. More information could be found in the travel reports (UM2022/26989/BOGO/18 and 29).
